html:
SMTO-LLM-0010 — Model stream contained invalid data

GUID: 25593465-a831-44a7-a1d1-9ac377f0e462
Slug: llm-stream-invalid-utf8
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: provider

What happened

  • Part of the model's reply contained bytes that aren't readable text, so SMTO stopped that reply. Nothing from it was carried out, and earlier finished steps are unchanged.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing, open the Main card, and select Check saved model. If the test also fails, the problem is in how the model server sends its replies, not in your task.
  2. If the check passes, on the stopped task, select Resume (or Continue task if that is what it shows). A fresh reply may arrive cleanly, and SMTO did not act on the unreadable one.
  3. If it happens again, ask the person who manages the model server to check that the server, and anything in front of it, sends replies as standard UTF-8 text. SMTO only accepts replies in that standard text format, and this reply broke that rule.

What success looks like

  • The task continues and the model's reply appears without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the model server, with the model and Endpoint you use. Changing languages or fonts on your computer won't help; the problem is in the data the server sent.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A line in the provider's SSE stream was not valid UTF-8 and was rejected before JSON parsing (llm_stream_invalid_utf8, stage sse_decode).

What this means

  • A received stream line could not be decoded as UTF-8. The text is rejected before JSON interpretation. This establishes invalid wire encoding, not a model reasoning failure or a missing language pack.

Why this can happen

  • At least one stream line contains an invalid UTF-8 sequence.

How to diagnose it

  • Have the provider operator check response encoding and any proxy transformations. Compare direct and proxied test responses without recording private model output.

How to fix it

  • Capture a small streaming request to the configured endpoint's /chat/completions and verify the body is UTF-8 text/event-stream from start to finish; check any proxy that re-encodes or rewrites the stream. Correct the provider or proxy encoding, then resume; this is a wire-encoding fault, not a model reasoning failure.
  • Ask the provider operator to check the stream format and byte limits with a small test request. Preserve prior tool receipts; do not replay completed operations.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A controlled stream decodes as UTF-8 from start to finish.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • The bounded stream decoder rejects the current response; it does not rewrite earlier tool receipts.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
